items.prompt:
Read the simile.

The pillow was as fluffy as a cloud.

What does this simile mean?
A) The pillow was very soft and puffy
B) The pillow was made of rain
C) The pillow was gray
D) The pillow floated away
items.answer: A) The pillow was very soft and puffy

steps: The simile compares the pillow to a cloud using "as."
Clouds look soft and puffy.
So the pillow was very soft and puffy, answer A.
solution.answer: A) The pillow was very soft and puffy

items.prompt:
Choose the antonym.

The path up the mountain was difficult.

Which word is an antonym (opposite) of "difficult"?
A) Hard
B) Easy
C) Long
D) Steep

steps: An antonym means the opposite.
"Difficult" means hard to do.
The opposite is "easy," answer B.

items.prompt:
Choose the synonym.

The enormous whale swam past the boat.

Which word is a synonym (same meaning) for "enormous"?
A) Tiny
B) Huge
C) Fast
D) Blue

steps: A synonym means the same thing.
"Enormous" means very big.
"Huge" means the same, answer B.

items.prompt:
Read the metaphor.

My dad is a bear before he has his morning coffee.

What does this metaphor mean?
A) My dad has brown fur
B) My dad is grumpy and gruff in the morning
C) My dad lives in the woods
D) My dad likes honey
items.answer: B) My dad is grumpy and gruff in the morning

steps: A metaphor says one thing IS another.
Dad is called "a bear" before coffee.
Bears can seem grumpy, so it means Dad is grumpy in the morning, answer B.
solution.answer: B) My dad is grumpy and gruff in the morning

items.prompt:
Read the idiom.

When I spilled the secret, my brother said I "let the cat out of the bag."

What does "let the cat out of the bag" mean?
A) Freed a real cat
B) Told a secret that was supposed to be kept
C) Made a big mess
D) Lost something important
items.answer: B) Told a secret that was supposed to be kept

steps: This is an idiom with a hidden meaning.
The sentence says "I spilled the secret."
The idiom means to reveal a secret, answer B.
solution.answer: B) Told a secret that was supposed to be kept

items.prompt:
Read the proverb.

Grandpa always says, "A penny saved is a penny earned."

What lesson does this proverb teach?
A) Pennies are worthless
B) Money you save is as valuable as money you earn
C) You should spend all your money
D) Only earn, never save
items.answer: B) Money you save is as valuable as money you earn

steps: A proverb teaches a lesson.
The saying compares saving a penny to earning one.
It teaches that saving money is just as good as earning it, answer B.
solution.answer: B) Money you save is as valuable as money you earn

items.prompt:
Read the sentence.

The crowded classroom was a beehive of buzzing voices and constant motion.

Which statement about this sentence is correct?
A) It is a simile, and it means the room was quiet
B) It is a metaphor, and it means the room was busy and full of activity
C) It is an idiom, and it means the room was empty
D) It is a proverb about hard work
items.answer: B) It is a metaphor, and it means the room was busy and full of activity

steps: There is no "like" or "as," so it is a metaphor, not a simile.
The room is called "a beehive of buzzing voices."
A beehive is busy and full of motion, so it means the room was busy, answer B.
solution.answer: B) It is a metaphor, and it means the room was busy and full of activity

items.prompt:
Read the adage.

Before Maria fixed her bike wrong twice, her uncle warned, "Haste makes waste."

Which sentence best explains the adage and fits the story?
A) Working fast is always best, so Maria should hurry
B) Rushing can lead to mistakes, so Maria should slow down and be careful
C) Bikes are hard to fix, so Maria should quit
D) Waste is good, so Maria should not worry about mistakes
items.answer: B) Rushing can lead to mistakes, so Maria should slow down and be careful

steps: "Haste" means hurrying and "waste" means ruined effort.
The adage means hurrying causes mistakes.
Maria fixed it wrong twice, so she should slow down, answer B.
solution.answer: B) Rushing can lead to mistakes, so Maria should slow down and be careful
